name: South Russia
native: Вооружённые силы Юга России (Vooruzhonnye sily Yuga Rossii)

predecessors.name: General Command of the Armed Forces of South Russia
predecessors.text: the Kuban (Ekaterinodar captured August 1918) and the south-eastern Don, where the General Command established on 31 August 1918 "performed government functions"

predecessors.name: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic
predecessors.text: land taken from the Soviets in 1919

successors.name: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic
successors.text: the Don, Kuban, North Caucasus, Lower Volga and Black Earth lands retaken by the Red Army, October 1919 to April 1920

successors.name: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic
successors.text: the Ukrainian lands retaken from December 1919

rulers.name: Anton Denikin (Commander-in-Chief, Armed Forces of South Russia)
Pyotr Wrangel (pravitel' of the Government of South Russia)

ledger.x: 1919, 8 January: South Russia is established by the White movement on the Don, the Kuban and the North Caucasus, under Denikin's Armed Forces of South Russia.

1919, May: the AFSR offensive forces the Red Southern Front to retreat; the Denikin page adds that in spring 1919 his forces "checked a major Red offensive in the Donbas region" and in May "a series of counter-offensives routed the Red armies".
1919, May: the AFSR offensive "forced the front to retreat from" Kharkov, Belgorod, Balashov and Tsaritsyn.

1919, May: the Southern Front opens along the Donbas and Kharkov as Denikin's counter-offensives rout the Red armies; zone drawn from the cities and regions the pages name (the Kursk-Orel-Voronezh belt, Donbas, Tsaritsyn).
1919, June: "In June 1919, after a fierce battle, Wrangel's troops stormed and captured the heavily fortified city" (Tsaritsyn, now Volgograd).
1919, 25 June: "On 25 June 1919, Denikin's Armed Forces of South Russia captured Kharkov, followed by Ekaterinoslav on 30 June."
1919, 30 June: Denikin's forces captured Kharkov on 25 June, "followed by Ekaterinoslav on 30 June" (Yekaterinoslav, now Dnipro).
1919, 31 July: "He took Poltava on July 31, Odesa on August 23, and Kyiv on August 31".
1919, 23 August: Denikin "took...

1919, 31 August: "... and Kyiv on August 31"; the Ukrainian-Soviet War page agrees ("on 31 August Anton Denikin's Volunteer Army established its positions in the city"), and the Southern Front page puts the front's loss of Kiev between August and October.

1919, September: the Southern Front gave up "Kiev, Odessa, Kursk, Voronezh, and Orel between August and October" and "through September and early October the front retreated to the north again", Kursk being lost in that retreat; the page gives no day (the Orel-Kursk operation of 11 October-18 November retakes it).
1919, 30 September: "on 30 September, Voronezh and Orel": the Whites take both; by October they are within 350 km of Moscow, South Russia's greatest extent.
1919, autumn: the remaining Ukrainian oblasts are inside the territory at the peak.
1919, 11 October to 18 November: the Red Southern Front retakes Orel, Kursk (Orel-Kursk operation) and Voronezh (13 October to 16 November).
1919, 24 November to 12 December: the Red Southern Front takes Kharkov, Sumy, Belgorod and Stary Oskol.
1919, 24 November to 12 December: the Red Southern Front takes Kharkov, Belgorod and Stary Oskol in the Kharkov operation.
1920, 3-10 January: the Red Southern Front takes Taganrog, Novocherkassk, Rostov-on-Don and Tikhoretsk and reaches the Sea of Azov.

1920, January: the Southern Front "pushed the Armed Forces of South Russia back to the Black Sea and North Caucasus by early 1920" (the Rostov-Novocherkassk operation, 3-10 January; the front was renamed the South-Western Front on 10 January 1920).
1920, winter: the rest of Ukraine falls to the Reds: "by 1920 all of Eastern and central Ukraine except Crimea was again in Bolshevik hands".
1920, 26-27 March: the Volunteer Army's remaining troops are evacuated from Novorossiysk to the Crimea.
1920, late March: the Southern Front ends on the mainland with the evacuation from Novorossiysk; only the Kuban Army (to April) and the Crimea remain.

1920, 4 April: the Government of South Russia is established in Sevastopol, successor to Denikin's South Russian Government ("set up in February 1920"); it adopted the name "Government of South Russia" officially on 16 August 1920 and France recognised it in August 1920.
1920, April: the capital moves to Sevastopol; the South Russia page says Wrangel "set up a new government in Sevastopol... in April".
1920, 18-20 April: the Kuban Army, which replaced the Caucasus Army on 29 January 1920, surrenders to the Red Army; the Kuban and the North Caucasus are lost.
1920, June: "In June 1920, Wrangel launched his last major offensive, the Northern Taurida Operation" and "his forces broke out of the Crimean bottleneck and captured a large territory to the north".

1920, 28 October: the Red Southern Front advances out of the Kakhovka bridgehead into Northern Taurida (Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol, Chongar, 28 October to 3 November), then through Perekop and Chongar (7-17 November).

1920, 28 October to 3 November: the Red Southern Front's "counteroffensive in northern Taurida between 28 October and 3 November" captured Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol and Chongar; the Perekop-Chongar operation followed on 7-17 November.

1920, 7-17 November: "Between 7 and 17 November it broke through Russian Army defenses on the Isthmus of Perekop" (the Lithuanian Peninsula, the Turkish Wall, Yushun and the Chongar positions), and Wrangel "initiated an evacuation of 146,000 people to Constantinople with the last boats departing on 16 November".
1920, 17 November: the fighting for Northern Taurida and the Crimea ends.
1920, 17 November: the Government of South Russia is dissolved after the loss of the Crimea; South Russia ends.

wars.name: Southern Front (Russian Civil War)
wars.outcome: Red victory: Orel, Kursk and Voronezh retaken October-November 1919, Kharkov December 1919, Rostov January 1920, Novorossiysk March 1920, the Kuban April 1920.

wars.name: Siege of Perekop
wars.outcome: Red victory: Perekop and Chongar broken 7-17 November 1920; evacuation of 146,000 people from Sevastopol to Constantinople by 16 November.

certainty.note: Civil-war fronts and cities, not lines; the oblasts are readings from the names on the pages.
